summary: Admit an approval-bound Russian Post formed-batch archive restore operation through the tenant-scoped API and operation receipt boundary.

impacts.evidence: The route resolves the active logistics account in the authenticated organization/workspace scope and uses a tenant-scoped operation receipt.
The operation carries only a provider batch reference and stores no customer PII.
OpenAPI adds POST /logistics/batches/archive/revert/{batch_id} with required idempotency and approval headers and a bounded account reference.
The operation adds no event contract and returns a normalized provider result.
A provider-neutral batch unarchive request, result port and capability are additive to SDK v1.
Existing operation_receipts persistence supports pending/completed normalized results; no migration is needed.
Runtime admission, account capability, approval and idempotency are default-deny and independently checked.
The route requires write-sensitive fulfillment.batch.unarchive approval bound to the account and batch reference.
The approval ID, digest and operation receipt preserve privileged-operation lineage without storing raw provider data.
A fresh receipt owns the single remote call; completed replays do not call the provider and pending outcomes block blind retry.
The adapter uses fixed HTTPS egress to the documented Russian Post archive-revert endpoint and one bounded batch reference.
The API distinguishes fresh results, completed replays and pending ambiguous outcomes without returning raw provider errors.
Disabling capability or runtime admission prevents new restore calls while existing receipt evidence remains available; provider-side archive operations stay separate.
Deterministic connector, HTTPS transport, API approval/idempotency, runtime admission, OpenAPI, SDK and frontend checks cover the operation.
